newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: IRISH FRUIT OF LOOM CHIEF FIGHTS FOR JOB.
newsitem.headline: IRISH FRUIT OF LOOM CHIEF FIGHTS FOR JOB.

text.p: Northern Ireland-based Fruit of the Loom managing director Willie McCarter applied for an injunction against a redundancy notice served on him by his American bosses, Irish media reported on Thursday.

The high-profile, Derry-born businessman, his brother John and finance director Seamus McEleney were served with redundancy notices by U.S. Fruit of the Loom Corporation which owns 100 percent of the Irish businesses.
The current dispute appears to have been growing since the beginning of the year when some of McCarter's responsibilities were transferred back to the U.S., media reports said.
In 1986, U.S. Fruit of the Loom bought McCarter's Ireland interests in Derry and Donegal from the McCarter family and Willie McCarter was appointed managing director of the Irish operations in 1987.
The company, which now has seven plants, two in Derry and the rest in Donegal, is one of the largest employers in manufacturing in Ireland with about 3,500 workers.

Media reports say files at the Company Records office show that Fruit of the Loom in Ireland slid into the red, recording a pre-tax loss of 13.5 million pounds in 1995 down from a profit of 5.8 million in 1994.
Tensions are understood to have emerged between the Irish and European management over repeated slumps in sales of Fruit of the Loom clothing which led to short time working in the Irish plants.
On Wednesday McCarter and his two colleagues, applied for injunctions against the redundancy notices in the High Court in Dublin.
The case will be heard in two weeks time.
McCarter is heavily involved in cross border relations and is chairman of the International Fund for Ireland.
